\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Clamped input query agrees with signed query]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.clamp_cX}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.clamp_cX}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.AllGood, Complexity.Meyer.cX, Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.sv, Complexity.Meyer.sv_sgn}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite
Boolean input, and let $A$ be a Boolean answer table. Suppose every local check in the
numerical encoding determined by $M,A,W,x$ and a Boolean sequence $x_b$ passes for every
time $t<2^W$, work index $a<2^W$, input index $j\le |x|+1$, and check type. Then for
every such time, every nonzero head movement $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and the answer table's
input-symbol queries, the signed query at offset $m$ equals the symbol query at index
$1$ with sign flag indicating whether $m$ is negative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input-cell consistency at a machine step]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.in_edge}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.in_edge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.AllGood, Complexity.Meyer.Correct, Complexity.Meyer.NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.SS, Complexity.Meyer.aE, Complexity.Meyer.avOf, Complexity.Meyer.avOf_ite, Complexity.Meyer.cX, Complexity.Meyer.claims_of_correct, Complexity.Meyer.clampedA, Complexity.Meyer.edge_c1, Complexity.Meyer.edge_c2, Complexity.Meyer.goodF, Complexity.Meyer.inOK, Complexity.Meyer.reads, Complexity.Meyer.sE, Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.sv, Complexity.Meyer.sv_sgn, Complexity.Meyer.symvA_NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.tvOf, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and
let $Ans$ be a Boolean answer table for selectors and time and space parameters. Suppose
every local checking condition in the finite tableau encoding is satisfied, and at time
$t$ the answer table correctly represents the machine configuration and scanned symbols.
If $t+1<2^W$ and $e$ is an integer with $-(|x|+1)\le e\le |x|$, write $c$ for the
machine configuration at time $t$ and let $m$ be its prescribed input-head movement when
$c$ is nonhalting. Then the encoded input symbols at times $t$ and $t+1$ agree at
positions $e$ and $e+1$ when $c$ is halted or $m=0$; for a right move they agree at
$e,e+1$ if the scanned input symbol is blank and the encoded symbol at the right
boundary is blank, and otherwise the symbol at time $t+1$ and position $e$ equals that
at time $t$ and position $e+1$; for a left move they agree at $e,e+1$ under the
analogous blank-boundary condition, and otherwise the symbol at time $t+1$ and position
$e+1$ equals that at time $t$ and position $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input boundary consistency]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.bd_edge}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.bd_edge}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.AllGood, Complexity.Meyer.Correct, Complexity.Meyer.NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.SS, Complexity.Meyer.avOf, Complexity.Meyer.bdOK, Complexity.Meyer.cX, Complexity.Meyer.claims_of_correct, Complexity.Meyer.clampedA, Complexity.Meyer.goodF, Complexity.Meyer.reads, Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.sv_sgn, Complexity.Meyer.symvA_NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.tvOf, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean input, let $x$ be a Boolean word,
and let $\mathrm{Ans}$ be a Boolean-valued table on machine selectors and two
natural-number indices. Suppose that every local checker condition holds for all times
$t<2^W$, addresses $a<2^W$, and input indices $j\le |x|+1$, and that at time $t$ the
table correctly represents the machine's state and output, work-tape reads within
distance $2^W-1-t$, and input reads within distance $|x|+1$. If $t+1<2^W$, then in the
machine configuration $c$ after $t$ steps, a halting state or a stationary input-head
move satisfies the boundary claim automatically. For a nonhalting configuration whose
transition moves the input head right, either the current input read is blank and the
table predicts no symbol at that position, or the table predicts no symbol at the right
boundary after $t+1$ steps; for a move left, the analogous alternative holds at the left
boundary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Far Input Positions Are Blank]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.RI_far}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.RI_far}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.RI, Complexity.Meyer.xhat_eq_none, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with
Boolean symbols, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let
$d\in\mathbb{Z}$. If $|d|>|x|+1$, then the input symbol seen from $c$ at offset $d$ is
absent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input-Rule Congruence]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.ruleI_congr}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.ruleI_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.Rd, Complexity.Meyer.ruleI}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with state set $S$, let $q\in\mathrm{Option}(S)$ be a
state or the halting marker, and let $\rho$ consist of an optional Boolean input symbol
and one optional Boolean symbol for each work tape. For an integer offset $d$ and
functions $f,g:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$ that agree at every integer,
the input-head update rule evaluated using $f$ equals the same rule evaluated using $g$.
\end{theorem}

alphabet, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. Suppose an atom assignment is good for

\end{theorem}

Boolean input, let $A$ be a Boolean answer table, and let $x_b$ be a Boolean sequence

$2^W$, all input indices at most $|x|+1$, and every check type. Then for every $t<2^W$,
the table answers all state-and-output queries correctly at time $t$, all work-tape
queries correctly at offsets satisfying $|d|+t\le 2^W-1$, and all input queries
correctly at offsets satisfying $|d|\le |x|+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness of the Numeric Checks]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.sound_numeric}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.sound_numeric}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.AllGood, Complexity.Meyer.NumVal_ans, Complexity.Meyer.SS, Complexity.Meyer.avOf, Complexity.Meyer.correct_all, Complexity.Meyer.goodF, Complexity.Meyer.tvOf, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean
string, let $W$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{Ans}$ assign a Boolean value to each
selector and pair of natural-number indices, and let $xb$ be a Boolean-valued function
on the natural numbers. Suppose that for every $t<2^W$, $a<2^W$, and $j\le |x|+1$, every
prescribed initialization, transition, work-tape, input, boundary, and final check is
satisfied by the numerical encoding determined by $\mathrm{Ans}$ and $xb$. Suppose also
that $xb(j)=x_j$ for every $j<|x|$. Then after $2^W-1$ steps, the machine $M$ is halted
and its output register records exactly one bit, equal to $1$.
\end{theorem}
